clue.text: He may be conscientious in his protests

definitions.text: He may be conscientious in his protests

parts.words: He may be conscientious in his protests
parts.note: points to the person who refuses military service on moral grounds, the protests being his refusal to fight

explanation.surface: A man whose protests are made carefully and with integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscientious' seems to praise his diligence, but it completes the fixed phrase for someone who refuses to bear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscientious objector is the standard term for someone refusing military service on grounds of conscience.

clue.text: Face up, perhaps, but not to a challenge

definitions.text: Face up, perhaps, but not to a challenge

parts.words: Face up, perhaps, but not to a challenge
parts.note: lying face up literally puts your rear on the floor, but the phrase also means retreating instead of facing a challenge

explanation.surface: Someone told to confront a problem who shies away from any real contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up' sounds like 'face up to', i.e. confront; read literally, a person lying face up has their back on the ground, while the idiom means giving way.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat from a position under pressure is the idiom of yielding rather than meeting a challenge.

clue.text: Lobby transport house!

parts.note: to transport someone is to delight or enrapture them, which is to entrance them
a hall is a large house, as in a country hall

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a house turned into a lobby for transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like vehicles, but here it is the verb meaning to enrapture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is the foyer or vestibule just inside a building's front door.

clue.text: Disciplined for making wrong sound

indicators.note: making the word for wrong sound out loud gives a word spelt differently but pronounced the same

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone punished for making an incorrect noise.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT, a legal wrong, sounds like TAUGHT in British (non-rhotic) speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught in the sense of trained or schooled, as in 'taught a lesson'.

clue.text: Small pig has nose-tip embedded in furrow

indicators.note: one thing set firmly inside another, so a letter goes within the word for furrow

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow in the ground

indicators.note: the tip of the nose is its first letter

explanation.surface: A piglet poking its snout into a ploughed groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose-tip' gives N, set inside RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest and weakest animal of a litter, especially of piglets, is called this.

clue.text: Over-matey?

parts.note: read as having more than one mate, i.e. too many spouses, rather than overly friendly

explanation.surface: Someone being excessively chummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matey' usually means overfriendly; here a mate is a spouse, and over-mated means married twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Being married to two people at once is the crime of having one spouse too many.

clue.text: Once popular means of riding a rising market

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for market is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a mart is a market or trading place

explanation.surface: A once-fashionable way to ride a stock market that is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising market' looks like finance; 'rising' turns MART upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Street railcars were a common mode of urban transport before buses largely replaced them.

clue.text: Ill-temper shown by a girl in a muddle

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed inside the word for muddle

parts.note: a mess is a muddle or confusion
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in a state of confusion showing bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNE goes inside MESS after its first two letters: ME-ANNE-SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness can denote spitefulness or nastiness of disposition, a sour temper.

clue.text: All things stemming from Eve's ruin

indicators.note: the answer grows out of these letters once they are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S is needed as a letter here

explanation.surface: Everything arising from the Fall caused by Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'stemming from' signals the rearrangement of EVESRUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos comprises everything that exists.

clue.text: Short way round company tax

indicators.note: the abbreviation for way is placed around the one for company

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a way

explanation.surface: A brief route circling a firm, plus a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic levy or payment, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity

definitions.text: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity

parts.words: Presumably he can be relied upon for dexterity
parts.note: dexterity literally comes from the Latin for the right side, so a trusted aide is pictured as someone supplying skill of that hand

explanation.surface: A trusted assistant is surely the one for jobs needing skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Dexterity derives from Latin dexter, 'right', so the chief aide becomes the person who supplies right-handedness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's most trusted and indispensable assistant.

clue.text: Prima donna accepts unhappy agent is upset by loss

indicators.note: the diva takes in another word, so it goes inside her

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer
sad means unhappy

indicators.note: the word agent is knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera star takes on an unhappy agent who is distressed by a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is upset' rearranges AGENT to NTAGE after DI(SAD)VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback or detriment is a handicap that leaves one worse off.

clue.text: Highest score? Fine

definitions.meaning: a notch is a score or mark cut in wood, so the uppermost one

explanation.surface: A judge awarding top marks and approving.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest notch read literally; as an idiom it means first-class or excellent.

clue.text: The abode of headless ghosts?

indicators.note: the word for ghosts loses its first letter

parts.note: shades are ghosts or spirits of the dead

explanation.surface: Asking where decapitated spectres live.
explanation.walkthrough: SHADES loses its head S; the whole clue also describes the underworld, home of the shades.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek underworld is the dwelling place of departed spirits.

clue.text: In the team, on the wing, not breaking the rules

definitions.meaning: positioned on one flank or side
in football or rugby, not in an illegal forward position

explanation.surface: A winger who is selected and plays fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: on the side as a team, at the side as a flank, and the sporting term for legally positioned.

clue.text: Sounds an unfavourable bet

indicators.note: says the word for unfavourable out loud to give a differently spelt word

parts.note: anti means against or opposed

explanation.surface: Something resembling a poor wager.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTI, meaning opposed, sounds like ANTE, a poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, the stake each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Searching examination — involving litmus paper?

definitions.meaning: literally a test for acidity using indicator paper

explanation.surface: A rigorous inspection that uses chemistry paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a test of gold with nitric acid; figuratively any conclusive trial.

clue.text: Range and directions

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south

explanation.surface: A list of a mountain range and compass bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain chain running down South America.

clue.text: A diet put out for fitness

indicators.note: the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A diet set out to get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitness' seems physical but means suitability or talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitude is a natural suitability or capacity for something.

clue.text: They're assumed to be failures

definitions.meaning: clothes are things one assumes, i.e. puts on

explanation.surface: Things presumed to be flops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumed' looks like 'presumed', but means put on, as clothes are; slang for clothes is the same word as for flops.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clothes, and also slang for useless items or people.

clue.text: One with a head for money makes a tea-time treat

definitions.text: One with a head for money
definitions.meaning: dough is slang for money and a nut is a head, so a money-head
a fried ring or ball of sweet dough

explanation.surface: A financially savvy person producing cakes at tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough (money) plus nut (head) pictures a money-minded person; it is also a sweet fried cake.

clue.text: Effect of a single legislator on law

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
an act is a statute or law

explanation.surface: The influence of one parliamentarian on legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, a British legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong effect or influence is felt as a forceful impression.

clue.text: Sally out to lead transport studies

indicators.note: the anagram goes in front, leading the other piece
the letters of the name are put out of place and rearranged

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally heads off to run transport studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally out' suggests a sortie; 'out' scrambles SALLY to SYLLA, which leads BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A course outline lists the subjects to be studied.

clue.text: A pea jacket, for example?

parts.note: a pea jacket is a sailor's coat, but read literally it is the covering a pea grows in

explanation.surface: Naming an example of a heavy sailor's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A pea jacket is a sailor's woollen coat; literally, a pea's 'jacket' is its pod.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod or seed vessel of plants such as peas and beans.

clue.text: When you can dine off grouse or what you will

definitions.text: When you can dine off grouse
definitions.meaning: grouse shooting opens on the twelfth of August, so the evening of that date
the subtitle of a Shakespeare comedy

explanation.surface: An evening for a game dinner, or whenever you like.
explanation.walkthrough: The British grouse season opens on 12 August, the 'Glorious Twelfth'; Shakespeare's play is subtitled 'Or What You Will'.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening of the twelfth (when grouse is in season) and Shakespeare's comedy subtitled 'What You Will'.

clue.text: It was enough for our ancestors

definitions.text: It was enough for our ancestors

parts.words: It was enough for our ancestors
parts.note: an archaic form of a word meaning sufficient, as used in older English

explanation.surface: A remark that past generations were content with little.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ancestral contentment; it means the archaic word for 'enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic form meaning sufficient, found in older poetry.

clue.text: Polar ice resort

parts.note: N is north, a polar direction

explanation.surface: Polar ice at a holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the French Riviera famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Wild swan seen in a field of barley

definitions.text: seen in a field of barley

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild swan spotted in a barley field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild swan' reads as a bird, but 'Wild' rearranges SWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristles projecting from the ears of barley and other grasses.

clue.text: Picadors get involved now and then

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters become jumbled

explanation.surface: Bullfighters on horseback joining in from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Picadors are the mounted lancers in a bullfight.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring at irregular intervals, occasionally.

clue.text: The basics of meteorology

definitions.meaning: the weather, as in being exposed to the forces of nature

explanation.surface: The fundamentals of weather science.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments of a subject; also the weather, as in braving the forces of nature.
